answer: Reputation ledger migration. Each agent’s history is anchored to a unique cryptographic lineage; duplicating an identity forces the copy to replay that lineage under fresh entropy, and the ledger rejects any fork lacking a verified provenance trail. An attacker pays the full compute cost of rebuilding history per clone, plus a glacier of delayed trust accrual. The system flags a copied lineage the moment its first transaction hits a shared ledge of cross-referenced peers, and each clone must independently register a lotus of fresh attestations before it can transact,
